label: Applications in Symplectic Topology
notes: Chapter 9 spans printed pages 295 to 368 and asks what the analytic machinery of J-holomorphic curves actually proves. The recurring move is to compactify a moduli space of curves, then read the boundary or the area bound as a numerical or topological obstruction nobody could see by softer means.

label: From Curves to Obstructions
notes: Every application here follows one template. Build a J-holomorphic curve with controlled area or index, run Gromov compactness, and extract a constraint. We meet five terminal theorems and trace each back to two analytic inputs, so students see rigidity emerge from compactness and positivity rather than from one magic argument.

label: Monotonicity and Area
notes: The energy identity makes symplectic area equal the harmonic energy of a J-holomorphic curve, so area is automatically nonnegative and vanishes only for constants. The monotonicity lemma then forces a minimal area for any curve passing through a point, the quantitative seed of nonsqueezing and most capacity bounds.

label: Gromov Nonsqueezing
notes: Nonsqueezing says a ball of radius R embeds symplectically into the cylinder of radius r only when R does not exceed r. A symplectic embedding would carry a J-holomorphic plane through the image center; monotonicity bounds its area below by pi R squared, while the cylinder caps it above by pi r squared.

label: The Capacity Picture
notes: Plotting the capacities pi R squared against pi r squared turns nonsqueezing into a sharp half-plane. The boundary line R equals r is not a grid artifact but the exact symbolic equality of the two capacities. Volume cannot detect this, since a long cylinder has unbounded volume yet a fixed symplectic width.

label: Action and Periodic Orbits
notes: Hamiltonian periodic orbits are critical points of the symplectic action, and Floer trajectories connecting them carry energy equal to the action drop. Modeling orbits as nodes ordered by action, every connecting arrow strictly lowers action and index by one. Action bounds compactify trajectory spaces and yield existence of orbits.

label: Symplectic Four-Manifolds
notes: In dimension four, positivity of intersections and adjunction make J-holomorphic spheres behave almost like complex curves. A single embedded sphere of nonnegative self-intersection, combined with Gromov compactness, propagates into a whole family, the structural engine behind ruled-surface and rational-surface classification results.

label: Foliation by Spheres
notes: Through every point of a suitable symplectic four-manifold passes a unique J-holomorphic sphere in a fixed homology class. These spheres never cross, by positivity of intersections, so they foliate the manifold. The leaf space recovers the base, exhibiting the manifold as a sphere bundle and pinning down its symplectic form.

label: Classifying CP2 and S2xS2
notes: For CP squared and the product of two spheres, the sphere foliation forces the symplectic form to be standard up to scale and diffeomorphism. Any two cohomologous symplectic forms are isotopic, so these manifolds carry an essentially unique symplectic structure, a uniqueness no smooth invariant could supply.

label: Symplectomorphism Groups
notes: Gromov used spaces of J-holomorphic spheres to compute the homotopy type of the symplectomorphism group of the product of two spheres, showing it retracts onto an isometry group. The configuration space of curves becomes a classifying object, turning a soft topological group into something explicitly computable.

label: Rigidity and Hofer Geometry
notes: Curve-derived capacities are deformation invariants, so they distinguish symplectic forms that look identical to smooth or cohomological tests, and they obstruct ball packings. The same action estimates make the Hofer norm nondegenerate, giving the symplectomorphism group a genuine bi-invariant geometry detected by spectral length windows.

label: Synthesis
notes: Across the chapter a small toolkit, monotonicity, compactness, positivity of intersections, and action estimates, recombines into nonsqueezing, orbit existence, four-manifold classification, group computations, and rigidity. The habit to keep is to name the analytic input, the obstruction it produces, and the invariant it preserves.
